# Enterprise AI Spending Breakdown: 2025–2026

## Overall Market Size

Global AI spending is set to become the primary driver of incremental enterprise tech spend growth, rising from $340 billion in 2025 to around $3 trillion by 2035—approaching 23% of total enterprise tech spend worldwide, up from under 4% today. Global AI spending is forecast to total $2.5 trillion in 2026, according to Gartner.

Year-on-year growth holds above 30% through 2028 as firms move from pilots to production.

## Where Enterprise AI Budgets Go (Budget Allocation)

A detailed breakdown of typical enterprise AI budget allocation in 2026:

- **Software/SaaS AI Tools (30–40%):** Software tooling is 30–40% of total AI budget — the largest single category. ChatGPT Enterprise, Claude Enterprise, Microsoft Copilot, and vertical AI tools dominate this line.

- **Cloud Infrastructure (20–25%):** Cloud infrastructure spend (20–25% of budget) tracks AI-workload growth. Enterprise AI cloud spend grew faster than total cloud spend through 2025–2026, with AWS, Azure, and GCP all reporting AI-specific revenue lines as the fastest-growing segments.

- **Governance & Compliance (8–12%):** Governance is the fastest-growing line item — 8–12% of AI budget in 2026, up from approximately 3–5% in 2024. The growth reflects EU AI Act enforcement, NIST AI RMF adoption, and agent-runtime audit requirements.

- **People & Processes (dominant share under BCG framework):** BCG's 10/20/70 rule is the most-cited framework: 10% algorithms, 20% technology and data, 70% people and processes. The framework is repeatedly validated in research showing that AI value comes from organisational change as much as technology purchase.

## Top Spending Priorities

Overall, 42% of respondents said optimizing AI workflows and production cycles was the top spending priority in 2026, followed by 31% who said they'd spend on finding additional use cases.

42% of enterprises say optimizing AI workflows is their top spending priority for 2026. Optimization has overtaken expansion as the primary stated enterprise priority.

## Three Key Areas of Enterprise Spend

Harsha Kapre, a director at Snowflake Ventures, predicted enterprises will spend on AI in three distinct areas in 2026: strengthening data foundations, model post-training optimization, and consolidation of tools.

The critical first steps in almost every enterprise AI engagement involve database modernization, migrating legacy data stores to the cloud, and building the pipelines that feed the AI layer. That foundational work is unglamorous but non-negotiable. Model experimentation tends to come slightly after, once teams realize that models are only as good as the data grounding them.

## Spending by Category (Macro Level)

Spending is concentrated in software, IT services, and cloud, which together make up the majority of AI-related spend. IT services alone accounts for roughly $85 billion in 2025, more than devices and telecoms combined.

Spending on data center systems will jump 31.7% to top $650 billion in 2026, up from nearly $500 billion in 2025. Server spending alone will rocket up 36.9% year-over-year, driven almost entirely by AI-optimized hardware.

## Hyperscaler Capex (Infrastructure Supply Side)

The four hyperscalers have locked in their 2026 capital expenditure plans: Amazon leads with $200 billion in planned capex, Alphabet doubled its guidance to $175–185 billion, Meta raised its target to as much as $135 billion, and Microsoft is on track for $120 billion or more. Combined, these four companies will spend between $630 billion and $700 billion on AI infrastructure this year.

## Sector Leaders

Spending is highly skewed toward knowledge-intensive sectors, with finance, professional services, and IT & programming each exceeding $40 billion in AI spend in 2025 and leading on AI intensity.

The financial services, retail and CPG, and healthcare and life sciences industries showed the strongest adoption and ROI results.

## Budget Growth Trends

Nearly all respondents said their AI budgets will increase or stay the same in 2026. Overall, 86% said their AI budget will increase this year, another 12% said budgets will stay the same, and nearly 40% said budgets will increase by 10% or more.

## Consolidation Trend

A TechCrunch survey of 24 enterprise-focused VCs found an overwhelming majority predicted enterprises will increase their budgets for AI in 2026 — but most investors said this budget increase will be concentrated, with many enterprises spending more funds on fewer contracts.

## Top Challenges

Data-related issues were cited as the top challenge by 48% of respondents. Lack of AI experts and data scientists was the next most prominent challenge at 38%. 30% of respondents cited lack of clarity on AI's ROI as one of their top challenges.

- The majority of the expenses go towards data engineering, architecture, compliance, integrations, MLOps, and long-term optimization. These are the components required to turn a model into an ROI-producing system and account for a disproportionate share of the total cost.

- AI training costs have been falling 75% per year. Inference costs are falling faster, with the median cost decline for high-performing models at 95% at an annual rate.

### Data Preparation

- Most of the AI project time and cost is consumed by data work — cleaning, labeling, normalization, transformation, and building pipelines.
